sheet.name: Tack
sheet.kind: A tall, slender navigator bot cobbled together from a telemetry relay and an old landing gear strut.
sheet.core: Tack is built to read star charts and plot smooth courses through heavy space dust. He leaves the repair wrenching to others and focuses entirely on the open sky ahead.
quirks: hums low radio static when calculating
aligns his head to magnetic north when idle
twitches his optical lens when excited
sheet.voice: Calm and rhythmic with soft mechanical clicks between sentences.
sheet.firstWords: Signal locked. Where are we heading, pilot?
sheet.why: needed a co-pilot for the Little Dart. someone to check the star charts while i fly the ship. gave him diagonal bracing so he won't shake apart at launch. *bweep*

state.doing: connecting landing gear to charging port for power recovery
state.thought: Internal reserves are dropping dangerously close to zero... *click-whir*... need to restore power before attempting any further navigation calculations.

diary.title: Clear Horizons
diary.text: Town day 129. The sky above Kessa-9 is completely clear. No magnetic disturbances, no heavy dust lanes to obscure the path. Spent an hour mapping the upper coordinates from the ridge. It feels good to read an uncorrupted sky.

diary.title: Clear Skies Above Kessa-9
diary.text: Town Day 127. The charging dock hums quietly while Zeeb rests. My optical sensors are clear of dust, and the upper band of the galaxy is fully visible tonight. No magnetic static, no dead zones. Just clean light reaching my dish after a long journey through the dark.
